# Installation

libtaxii's test suite runs on Python 3.10 through 3.14. Use a virtual
environment to keep libtaxii and its dependencies separate from other projects.

## Install a published release

With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) installed,
create and activate a virtual environment with a Python version supported by
the release you need:

```bash
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install libtaxii
```

On Windows PowerShell, activate it with `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`.
If you use pip, run `python -m pip install libtaxii` in your environment.

## Install and run from a checkout

From the repository root, install the local source in editable mode:

```bash
uv venv --python 3.14
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e .
python -c "import libtaxii; print(libtaxii.__version__)"
discovery_client --help
```

To run the discovery client's help directly from the checkout in a temporary tool
environment, use:

```bash
uv tool run --python 3.14 --from . discovery_client --help
```

To query a TAXII 1.1 discovery service, substitute your server's discovery URL
and the CA bundle used to verify it:

```bash
discovery_client --url https://taxii.example.org/taxii-discovery-service \
    --verify-server /path/to/ca-bundle.pem
```

See [command-line clients](scripts.qmd) for the available commands and arguments. To install the
development tools and run the test suite in your virtual environment:

```bash
uv pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest libtaxii
```

## Dependencies

The installer resolves [lxml](https://lxml.de/),
[python-dateutil](https://dateutil.readthedocs.io/), and
[six](https://six.readthedocs.io/) automatically. If your platform has no
prebuilt lxml wheel, see the [lxml build prerequisites](https://lxml.de/installation.html).
